title: Artifact for "Limits of Metamorphic Testing for Object-Level Authorization: Temporal Reachability, Oracle Admissibility, and Measurement Resolution"
description: Reproducibility artifact accompanying the JISA submission. It contains (i) the raw experimental records --- the scenario/configuration study, a real-system cell study across Gitea 1.22.6, Gogs 0.14.3 and GitLab 17.11.7, a three-arm paired recrawl study on a pinned Gogs 0.14.3 instance, execution of the published relations on the native engine, and a seeded positive control; (ii) the analysis pipeline that recomputes every number, table and figure in the paper from those records, under both admissible rules for the *unknown* cells; and (iii) the LaTeX manuscript source. Running `bash reproduce.sh` regenerates all outputs and the PDF; `bash verify_artifact.sh` asserts SHA-256 integrity of every raw record and byte-reproducible output. No number in the paper is hand-typed; all figures are vector (no AI-generated pixels). This package corresponds to the revised manuscript archived as tag `access-resubmission-v24` (25 pages, 22 tables, three vector figures).
notes: Package built from tag `artifact-v24` of https://github.com/ubfbuz3/JISA, which points to the same commit as the manuscript tag `access-resubmission-v24` cited in the paper's Data availability statement, so the archived code and the archived manuscript PDF are the ones the paper refers to. The creator list follows the manuscript byline. Earlier versions of this artifact keep their own records in this Zenodo concept (artifact-v1, artifact-v18, artifact-v18.1, artifact-v19, artifact-v20, artifact-v23). This version supersedes artifact-v23, which shipped a LaTeX source package built before the final text (a 309-word abstract and a Data-availability pointer to the previous tag) even though the manuscript sources in that tag were final; the package in this version carries the final sources and is bound to them by provenance/SUBMISSION_SOURCE_SHA256.json. Review correspondence and internal tracking notes are deliberately not part of this package. The concept DOI always resolves to the newest version; this record's own version DOI is the one Zenodo prints on the record page.
